entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Paulus Castrensis was a prominent Italian jurist who played a pivotal role in shaping the legal landscape of 14th-century Europe.

Born into a family of minor nobility in Verona, Castrensis studied law under the tutelage of the renowned jurist, Baldassare de Bazzano. His academic prowess and intellectual curiosity led him to become one of the most respected legal scholars of his time.

Castrensis's magnum opus, the 'Commentaria in Codicem Justiniani', a comprehensive interpretation of Justinian's Code, became a foundational text in the study of Roman law. His work had a profound impact on the development of medieval law, influencing the likes of Dante Alighieri and Petrarch.

Despite his significant contributions to the field, Castrensis's life was cut short when he died in 1447 at the age of 50. His legacy, however, lived on, as his work continued to shape the course of legal history.

As a testament to his enduring impact, Castrensis's name has become synonymous with Italian legal scholarship, and his influence can still be felt in the halls of academia today.
